title: Tiered credit → hire conversion lab
overview: Working hypothesis: convert a proportion of customer tiered-credit balances into time-limited 'credit-to-hire' reserves that fund short-term contractor capacity instead of full-time hires. This sheet models the headcount equivalence, marginal unit economics, and sensitivity to list-price changes across three pricing regimes.
model_summary: Approach: map credit dollars to GPU-hour equivalents, then to FTE-equivalents for roles (SRE/Platform/Support). Use per-role utilization multipliers (how many GPU-hours one FTE sustainably supports per month). Run three price scenarios (base, -20% price compression, +15% premium) and three demand trajectories (flat / +30% / -25%) to surface breakpoints at which hiring is preferable to funding contractor pools.
assumptions:
- Credit currency = net revenue-equivalent dollars after discounts.
- Base list token price per 1k tokens = $0.30 (effective GPU-hour mapping 0.045 GPU-hours per 1k tokens).
- GPU-hour market cost (internal blended) = $2.40/h.
- One FTE (infra-heavy SRE) covers ~210 GPU-hours/month of steady-state operational throughput for our workload mix. Platform eng coverage = 160 GPU-hrs/month. Support/CS escalation engineer = 120 GPU-hrs/month.
- Contractor pool burn efficiency = 0.85x of FTE (overhead/coordination).
- Hiring lead time (offer→ramp) = 10 weeks; contractor provisioning can be near-immediate (2 weeks).
- Budget horizon = 12 months for this experiment.

calculation_notes: Step 1: convert credit bucket into GPU-hours: GPU-hours = credit_dollars / blended_gpu_hour_cost. Step 2: FTE-equivalents = (GPU-hours * contractor_efficiency) / role_gpu_hours_per_FTE. Step 3: compare marginal cost of hiring (annualized fully-loaded comp converted to monthly) vs. using contractor credit pool (credit dollars consumed). Note: hiring introduces fixed tail risk (severance/attrition), contractors return to zero-cost when credits exhausted.
scenarios: Scenario A - Base pricing (0% change), demand flat: credit pool $1.2M → ~500k GPU-hours → supports ~11 SRE FTE months (over year ~9 FTE avg due to seasonality). Recommendation: temporary contractor pool preferred until utilization persists >9 months.

Scenario B - Price compression (-20% list): credits needed per GPU-hour rise (effective credit purchasing power falls). Same $1.2M buys ~400k GPU-hours → supports ~8 SRE FTE months. Hiring becomes less attractive as credits buy less. Suggest stricter hiring gating and accelerated quantization adoption to stretch credits.

Scenario C - Price premium (+15% list): credits buy more GPU-hours (~575k). This increases FTE-equivalent headroom to ~13 SRE FTE months. If demand growth materializes (+30%), hiring a small core (2-3 FTEs) combined with contractor overlay is economically defensible to reduce ramp friction.
sensitivity_results:
Short summary table (key breakpoints):
- Hiring breakeven (12-month horizon) for SRE: when expected sustained monthly GPU-hours > 170 per new hire AND credits per month < $40k (base).
- Price compression (-20%) moves breakeven upward by ~25% credit burn; i.e., you need ~25% longer demand persistence to justify hiring.
- Demand spike (+30%) accelerates break-even: 3–4 months of sustained spike triggers hire vs contractor.
Numeric example: base credits = $100k/mo buys ~41.6k GPU-hrs -> equivalent to ~5 SRE FTE-months; converting to hires: 5/ (12 months) -> ~0.42 new FTE sustained; hiring only if expected to persist >=8 months.
recommended_action: 1) Create a 6-month pilot: convert up to $600k of tiered credits into a contractor reserve managed by Solutions Eng and SRE lead. 2) Define explicit trigger rules: hire if contractor pool average utilization > 85% for 3 consecutive months AND forecasted demand delta > +15% for 3 months. 3) Implement a price-monitor (weekly) to track list-price movement; if list price compresses >10% sustain, freeze conversion and re-evaluate. 4) Build a light dashboard (Finance + Platform) showing credit burn rate, GPU-hour consumption, contractor FTE-equivalents, and hiring trigger status.
key_risks:
- Over-conversion: locking credits into contractors that underutilize forces cost without strategic benefit.
- Price volatility: sudden compression makes contractor reserves economically wasteful vs. hiring freeze.
- Operational overhead: managing many short-term contractors increases PM/engineering coordination costs.
- Hiring mis-timing: ramped hires with demand drop create fixed-cost tail risk.
next_steps:

- Engineering to instrument GPU-hour signaling in the Console (owner: Ravi) — ETA: 4 weeks.
- Finance to carve a trial credit tranche and track separately (owner: Amelia) — immediate.

- If pilot shows >85% utilization for 3 months, recruit 1–2 permanent hires to replace persistent contractor load.
notes: This is intentionally conservative on FTE per GPU-hour to account for platform complexity and cross-team overhead. The model intentionally isolates operational coverage decisions (SRE/Platform/Support) from product-sustained growth hires (sales/R&D). Further work: integrate with product-led revenue forecasts to map credit inflows to top-line and create a continuous policy instead of manual tranche decisions.
